title: GMV's defence, aerospace, healthcare and transport verticals are on record but its platform stack is not
content:
GMV's row lists four verticals — defence, aerospace, healthcare and transport — and records its platform stack as "not researched". Vertical fit is therefore the entire case for its presence in the priority-4 pool, and vertical fit alone cannot carry a lead: it says a firm serves buyers with the right problems, not that the firm has room or reason to place a new component.

The rank itself came from a mechanical rescore of a provisional v2 tail row, using size and slot occupancy only. No v3 evidence was gathered, which is what the flag means by "DERIVED, NOT SCORED ON v3", and it is why the priority field carries an unrun OSS-portfolio screen rather than a verdict.

For a firm working in defence and transport, the screen is also the cheapest way to learn something decision-relevant: what a systems house of this kind already standardises on tends to be visible in its published portfolio, and that is exactly the input the current record lacks.

description: Vertical fit is the whole case for the row; priority 4 was assigned mechanically from size and slot occupancy, and the OSS-portfolio screen is the first real evidence step available.
